title: Prefill tactics weekly snippets — kernel ripple & KV shadow
content:
Week: 2029-06-03 -> 2029-06-05
Owners: Aisha (notes), Tomás (kernel), Maya (KV), Ethan (batching)
Attendees: Tomás, Maya, Ethan, Aisha, Priya (SRE), Jin (perf)

Summary:
- This short sync focused on next-step tactics for prefill/coalescing behavior after the most recent kernel patch (PR 2145). We validated a smaller-than-expected ripple in tail latency for long-sequence prompts and sketched an approach to isolate KV shadow ingress as a likely cause.
- Ran two quick benches on the 4xA100 cluster and one mixed-traffic staging run (see linked GH bench artifacts).

Key observations:
1) Kernel patch impact (PR 2145):
   - Median latency: unchanged (~16ms per token for gpt-medium-optimized path).
   - 95th/99th: +3–7% on sequences >1k tokens when prefill was enabled. Not visible for short-chat flows.
   - Hypothesis: the new scheduling handoff increases contention for the prefill sharder for very long sequences (ticket SRV-1427).

2) KV shadow / prefill ingress:
   - KV hit-rate in shadow mode measured at 62% for common prefixes; however, there is a choke at the admission queue when many large-prefill requests arrive concurrently.
   - Admission queue length shows periodic spikes that correlate with 99th latency blips on the kernel side.

3) Batching heuristics:
   - Current dynamic batcher is merging prefill and inference-only requests aggressively. For mixed workloads we see tokenization and memory-copy overheads spike when batch size >64.
   - Suggested micro-optimization: separate prefill-only batches from live decode batches for short-responders.

Decisions / Short-term plan (this week):
- Isolate prefill admission: add a per-sharder soft-cap to hold prefill inflight at 2000 tokens equivalent (Maya) — target PR by 2029-06-07.
- Kernel scheduling probe: instrument additional per-core contention counters and export to perf dashboard (Tomás + Jin) — instrumentation by 2029-06-06.
- Batcher split experiment: run A/B on staging where prefill requests are pinned to a dedicated batching lane for 24 hours (Ethan) — start 2029-06-08.
- Quick rollback plan: if 99th latency worsens by >10% during experiments, auto-fallback to previous kernel behavior via routing policy for dedicated pools (Aisha to coordinate with SRE).

Data & Bench notes:
- Bench harness: mixed-chat-1000 (50% prefill-heavy), 6h run. Key numbers (median / 95th / 99th):
   - baseline kernel: 15.8ms / 53ms / 120ms
   - patched kernel: 16.1ms / 56ms / 128ms
   - staging A (prefill-lane): 15.9ms / 50ms / 115ms (promising)
- KV shadow metrics: ingress spikes at 11:07, 12:47 local; backlog reached 84 concurrent prefill tickets (seen in /metrics/prefill/queue-length).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should prefill admission be size-aware (tokens) or request-count-aware? Tradeoffs discussed: token-based is fairer for long prompts but adds accounting overhead.
- How to signal fallbacks across Dedicated vs Hosted? Routing policy semantics need to be explicit (Aisha to draft short policy text).
- Is there value in a fast-path kernel variant for short-chat that bypasses prefill for requests <64 tokens? (Pro: reduces copy overhead; Con: increases path divergence).

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: prototype per-sharder prefill soft-cap (PR + bench) — due 2029-06-07.
- Tomás: add contention counters to kernel and wire into perf dashboard; open GH PR for review — due 2029-06-06.
- Ethan: implement batching lane split and schedule 24h A/B in staging; report latency/cost delta — due 2029-06-09.
- Aisha: draft routing fallback policy and notify SRE on rollback runbook — due 2029-06-06.
- Jin: run microbench focused on memory copy perf with and without prefill separation; share profile flamegraphs — due 2029-06-08.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If per-sharder soft-cap helps but causes throughput drop, consider a tiny local cache warmup window (50ms) that accepts first prefill only and defers the rest.
- Could also explore tiny LRU at the admission point to bias repeated prefixes.
- Keep an eye on cost shift: batcher split may increase total GPU-seconds if small batches go up. Need to coordinate with cost/finance for experimental budgeting.

Meeting attachments & references:
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145 (kernel patch)
- Bench run: s3://redwood-bench/mixed-chat-1000/2029-06-04/
- JIRA: SRV-1427 (kernel contention), SRV-1432 (prefill admission)

Next sync: 2029-06-10 small-window async update; full group recap 2029-06-14.

End of snippet.
